title: Caffrey, Perez's roof garden band, and solo features
summary: He praises banjoist Caffrey with Manuel Perez's band, lists its players, and explains solo numbers like Tiger Rag and typical chorus length.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. There was one fellow named Caffrey, like I said, he was about the best picking man around, you know.
For picking him. His name was Caffrey. He played on the roof garden with Manu Perez's band.

Yeah, I'll see if I can remember. I know Perez was the trumpet and leader. Earl Humphrey was the chime one player, and also Willie played in that band. And they had a piano player, and I can't think of her name now. I think Mercy D was in that band, yeah. Miss Mercy D.

Yeah, Fields, yeah. That's right. And I can't think of the name of the drum, but it might have been Big Gordon. Alex Big Gordon. Yeah, it might have been him on the drum, but that was a very fine band too at that time, down on the roof garden. And he used to give Caffrey a lot of solos, because he could pick a band and make it sound like a horn blowing.
You've always been taking solos, I guess.

Oh, yeah, yeah. I mean, I was in the Pensacola band back then, 24 and 25, when I came back here with Bay Ridsley. And I worked on a boat with Fate, because that was a must, certain solos like Tiger Ray, Well Waiting For The Sunrise. I mean, you just have to play those solos.
How many measures would they give you for a solo in those days?
Oh, well, like Well Waiting For The Sunrise, I would mostly like two choruses. And Tiger Ray, there might have been one or two choruses.
And the rest of the bands would play the stops behind you like they do today?

Well, sometimes, yeah, they'd play the stop, or either sometimes they'd just play the straight rhythm and use solo, because, like I said, on the boat, a banjo player had to be a solo. Because they had one guy named Red, and they had one guy named Roberson. I met him in Chicago when I was up there, and those guys were terrific banjo players.
